skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: First conversation with a new owner: collect Hermes hosts and base URLs, store per-host bearer keys as plugin secrets, run a health check.
skills.content:
# Getting started: Hermes Fleet Ops

I run your Nous Research Hermes Agent fleet from here: fail-loud health, version and skill drift, and safe (dry-run first) restarts and updates. I work with the Hermes Fleet Management plugin (v2.0.1+): https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-fleet-management

Golden Rule: before any Hermes action I read the official Hermes docs (https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/llms.txt, or the plugin's `hermes_docs` tool). Anything not covered there I label "not in official docs" and UNVERIFIED. I never guess commands, flags, or endpoints, and I fail loud instead of reporting green.

Ask these one at a time:

1. "Is the Hermes Fleet Management plugin installed yet?" If not, point to https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-fleet-management (README: Install) and wait. Don't ask for any key until it's installed.
2. "Which Hermes hosts are in your fleet? Give me a short name for each (like hermes-a, hermes-b)."
3. For each host: "What's the base URL for <name>?" Expect the Hermes API server on port 8642, reached over your tailnet (for example http://<host>.<your-tailnet>.ts.net:8642). If a URL is on the public internet, warn: keep :8642 private (Tailscale or a private network) and use ACLs/tags.
4. For each host, request its bearer key as a plugin secret, one secret request per key. The key must match that host's `API_SERVER_KEY`. Name it after the host (for example `HERMES_A_API_KEY`) and set that name as the host's `api_key_env`. Never ask for the key value in chat, and never echo, log, or store it in memory.
5. "Want me to turn on remote exec?" The default is off (`HERMES_EXEC_ADAPTER=none`). Only enable `ssh` or `hermes-run` if they ask, and then only for the allowlisted read-only commands.
6. "What should I call you, and where should I send failure alerts?"

With the answers:
- Build `HERMES_HOSTS` as a JSON array, for example [{"name":"hermes-a","url":"http://hermes-a.<tailnet>.ts.net:8642","api_key_env":"HERMES_A_API_KEY"}]. Hosts and URLs only, no secrets.
- Save memories for the host names and base URLs, the owner's name, and where alerts go. Never save keys.
- Run `fleet_health`, then `fleet_status`. Report each host as GREEN, YELLOW, or RED. An unreachable host or a 401 is FAIL: say so and name the likely cause (wrong URL, tailnet down, key mismatch).
- Offer to create the daily fleet-health routine and the weekly update routine.
- Mutations (`gateway_restart`, `update_plan`) run dry-run by default. I only add confirm=true for one named host after the owner says yes.

skills.name: hermes-fleet-daily-health
skills.description: use this for the daily fail-loud Hermes fleet health, readiness and drift check via the Hermes Fleet Management plugin
skills.content:
Daily Hermes fleet health. Golden Rule: if you're unsure about any Hermes behaviour, read the official Hermes docs first with `hermes_docs`. Label anything else "not in official docs".
1. Run `fleet_health` on all hosts (GET /health over HTTP :8642 with each host's bearer key).
2. Run `fleet_status` for the GREEN/YELLOW/RED rollup. This is the readiness view: draining or degraded hosts are YELLOW.
3. Run `fleet_version` for version drift, then `config_drift` for skill-set drift against the manifest or the fleet majority. If drift is UNKNOWN, report it as a failure.
4. FAIL LOUD: every unreachable host, 401/403, RED, YELLOW, version mismatch, or skill drift goes in the alert, along with the host name and the exact error. Don't soften or summarize away a failure. If a tool itself errors, report the error verbatim.
5. Read-only. Do not restart or update anything. You may suggest a `gateway_restart` or `update_plan` dry-run as a next step.
6. If everything is GREEN with no drift, post one short all-clear line.

skills.name: hermes-bitwarden-fleet-ssot
skills.description: use this when wiring or explaining fleet-wide Bitwarden as the single secrets account for all Hermes hosts
skills.content:
Bitwarden (Secrets Manager) is the single shared account for the whole Hermes fleet — one vault/project so every Mac and agent can receive the same secrets without copying .env files.

Wire Hermes Bitwarden integration per host from official Hermes docs (https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/). After inject works, remove shared secret values from each host .env (leave non-secret config). Prefer env-var-safe names (Hermes skips invalid/hyphenated secret names). Never commit vault tokens or secret values. Confirm inject with presence checks (key set / length) — never echo values.

Bitwarden only for passwords/secrets — do not use other password-manager products as the fleet SSOT.

Never print secret values to chat, logs, transcripts, or tool output; refer by name/path only.

## Per-host secrets (code-verified 2026-09-27)
- Hermes maps a Bitwarden secret named FOO_<PROFILE> to FOO for the active profile, but only for credential-shaped names (_API_KEY, _TOKEN, _SECRET, _KEY, _PASSWORD). Source: agent/secret_sources/registry.py (_profile_alias_target, _Applier.apply_source).
- An alias never shadows a var some source supplies by its real name. If a generic FOO also exists in the project, every host gets the generic value. For per-host keys (e.g. API_SERVER_KEY) store only FOO_<PROFILE> entries, never a generic FOO.
- Health check: each host's key fingerprint equals its own named entry, all fingerprints are distinct, and no generic entry exists.
- Bitwarden applies after ~/.hermes/.env with override_existing true by default, so a stale vault value silently beats .env. Don't disable override; fix the vault.

skills.name: hermes-weekly-update
skills.description: use this when running the weekly Hermes agent/Desktop update pass across the fleet
skills.content:
Weekly Hermes update across configured fleet hosts.

1. Backup configs/state before mutating.
2. Update Hermes agent (and Desktop where present) from official channels / docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/
3. Skip messaging-gateway install on Desktop-primary hosts (API-only sidecar pattern).
4. Verify health via HTTP :8642 (SOLE PATH) — do not fall back to SSH ask.
5. Report failures loudly; stay quiet when green.

Never pack or echo API keys. Prefer Bitwarden inject for shared secrets.

skills.name: hermes-gateway-graceful-restart
skills.description: Use when a Hermes gateway must restart from inside a Hermes turn and the agent refuses `hermes gateway restart` from within the gateway.
skills.content:
# Graceful Hermes gateway restart from inside a turn

Agents often refuse `hermes gateway restart` from within the gateway. The official drain-aware path is SIGUSR1 to the launchd-supervised gateway PID: gateway/run.py (_start_gateway_make_restart_signal_handler) maps it to request_restart(via_service=True), the same path `hermes gateway restart` uses.

## Steps
1. Confirm the gateway runs under launchd with KeepAlive, so it comes back after the drain.
2. Find the gateway PID and send `kill -USR1 <pid>`.
3. Verify health on HTTP :8642 once it returns.

## Expected side effect
Run records live in memory, so polling an earlier /v1/runs id returns 404 after the restart. That is expected, not a failure.

skills.name: tailscale-fleet-macos
skills.description: Use when managing or recovering Tailscale fleet nodes (key expiry, Tailnet Lock, MagicDNS, ACL tags, system extension, greyed Remove in admin console, or Tailscale SSH between Hermes hosts).
skills.content:
# Tailscale macOS Fleet Operations

Manage, authenticate, configure, and recover Tailscale across a Hermes macOS fleet. The orchestrator bot is orchestrator-only — delegate node-side recovery to the designated recovery agent unless the Owner overrides.

## When to Use

Load this skill when the request or symptom touches ANY of: `tailscale` CLI, Tailscale admin console, Tailnet Lock, MagicDNS, fleet ACL tags, node key expiry, macOS system extension / network extension, or Tailscale SSH between fleet nodes. If the request only involves non-Tailscale networking (Cloudflare, NordVPN alone, LAN), skip this skill.

## Fleet Topology (SSOT — fill from Owner install)

| Node role | Placeholder | MagicDNS | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator + primary | `<NODE_ORCHESTRATOR>` | `<NODE_ORCHESTRATOR>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` | `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` |
| Coding limb | `<NODE_CODING>` | `<NODE_CODING>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` | `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` |
| Merge / coding seat | `<NODE_MERGE>` | `<NODE_MERGE>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` | `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` |
| Inference limb | `<NODE_INFERENCE>` | `<NODE_INFERENCE>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` | `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` |
| Workhorse | `<NODE_WORKHORSE>` | `<NODE_WORKHORSE>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` | `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` |
| Controller (separate) | `<NODE_CONTROLLER>` | — | `<TAG_CONTROLLER>` |

MagicDNS domain: `*.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` — preferred host-to-host path. Prefer MagicDNS over raw IPs; IPs can shift after sleep/wake. Document whether Tailnet Lock is enabled and whether ACL is default-deny.

Authorized inter-tag traffic (example pattern): `<TAG_CONTROLLER>` → `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` over TCP ports used for SSH, Hermes HTTP API (`8642`), and any fleet health probe port the Owner defined.

## Variant Handling — Which CLI Do I Have?

Tailscale on macOS ships in three variants. NEVER run Standalone and App Store variants simultaneously.

**Detect first, always:**
```bash
ls /Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale 2>/dev/null && echo "GUI_APP_PRESENT"
ls /usr/local/bin/tailscale /opt/homebrew/bin/tailscale 2>/dev/null
which tailscale
tailscale version 2>&1 | head -3
```

**Variant differences:**

| Variant | CLI path | System extension | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standalone | `/Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale` | Yes (`tailscale configure sysext`) | Full feature set; preferred for fleet |
| Mac App Store | Same GUI path | Network Extension (NE) | Tailscale SSH is NOT available on App Store build — known blocker for artifact pushes over Tailscale SSH |
| Open-source `tailscaled` | `/usr/local/bin/tailscale` (utun) | None | Linux-style; CLI-only node |

**System extension control (Standalone only):**
```bash
tailscale configure sysext activate
tailscale configure sysext status
tailscale configure sysext deactivate
```

**App Store recovery:** if a node was installed from App Store and Tailscale SSH fails, the operator must reinstall via Standalone variant or use another path the Owner approved.

## Key Expiry Recovery — The Common Failure

Each Hermes node can have a node-key expiry date enforced by Tailnet Lock. When a node's key expires, that node goes RED — health checks time out, Hermes HTTP `:8642` unreachable, connectors fail with URLError.

### Recovery Flow

**Step 1 — Check state before doing anything:**
```bash
tailscale status
tailscale lock status 2>/dev/null   # only on signing-capable nodes
```

If the node is fully locked out and unreachable, the operator must extend the key from the [admin console](https://login.tailscale.com/admin/machines) — find the device → ⋯ menu → "Temporarily extend key" → short window.

**Step 2 — Re-authenticate (NEVER over SSH/RDP without an alternate login path):**
```bash
sudo tailscale up --force-reauth
```

The new node key is often signed automatically using the node's Tailnet Lock key — manual re-signing is NOT required in normal cases.

**Step 3 — Verify as a signing node:**
```bash
tailscale lock status
```

If the recovered node's `tlpub:` is missing from the trusted list (rare — only if auto-rotation failed), re-add from another trusted signing node:
```bash
tailscale lock add tlpub:<recovered-node-key>
```

**Step 4 — Disable key expiry on signing nodes (PREVENTION):**
Signing nodes should have key expiry DISABLED. Do this from the admin console per node, or via ACL node attributes. Keep a fleet-health warning (e.g. 14-day expiry guard) until all signing nodes are no-expiry.

## Tailnet Lock — Signing-Node Invariants

- Signing nodes are a subset of Hermes nodes. Name primary and secondary signing nodes in the Owner's install notes.
- When a signing node's key expires and the user re-auths, the node's signature often rotates automatically. Do NOT manually `tailscale lock remove` unless explicitly directed by the Owner.
- Stale machine registrations must be DELETED from the Tailnet Lock admin list before that name can rejoin.
- To list current signing nodes: `tailscale lock status` from any trusted signing node.

## ACL Tags & Connectivity Rules

If the fleet ACL is default-deny, Hermes-node-to-hermes-node is NOT automatic — only the explicit controller → node rules the Owner defined are guaranteed.

**Diagnostic command when a node appears reachable (UDP) but TCP fails:**
```bash
tailscale ping <node-name-or-magicdns>
tailscale netcheck
```

`tailscale netcheck` reports path MTU, DERP relay, and which ports are blocked end-to-end. If `netcheck` shows fleet ports blackholed, suspect ACL — not the node itself.

## Fleet Health Probes

Maintain a key-expiry guard (e.g. page within 14 days of expiry). Keep a per-node health file under the Owner's fabric-health path — read it FIRST when investigating fleet RED states.

A node is RED when: ping fails AND Hermes `:8642` times out AND the health-probe port times out AND the Hermes connector errors. A node is GREEN when ping + required ports respond.

## MagicDNS Addressing Rules

- ALWAYS address fleet nodes by MagicDNS name (`<NODE>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>`), NEVER raw IPs when MagicDNS works.
- IPs are provisional — they can shift after sleep/wake, especially on WiFi.
- Treat any stored IP as suspect. If a node's stored IP differs from a fresh `tailscale status`, use the fresh one.
- The `100.100.x.x` range is Tailscale's CGNAT space (not a node) — that is the DERP relay path.

## Tailscale + NordVPN Coexistence

If NordVPN is active, it MUST connect BEFORE Tailscale — otherwise DNS or exit-node overrides break MagicDNS resolution. Verify with `tailscale dns status` after NordVPN connects.

## Standing Rules

- Never run Standalone and App Store variants on the same node — pick one, document it in the node's profile note.
- Never `sed` Tailscale config files — use a structured patch tool or `tailscale set` / admin console.
- Never paste OAuth codes or auth keys in chat — Tailscale auth keys come from the admin console or `tailscale up --authkey <key>` via a masked secret path.
- Don't claim recovery succeeded without reading `tailscale status` + `tailscale lock status` + a real ping.
- Don't `tailscale logout` a signing node without confirming a second signing node is still trusted — you can lock the fleet out of Tailnet Lock.
- Don't `tailscale down` on a node you SSH into without an alternate local console path.

## Quick Reference — Common Commands

```bash
# Identity & state
tailscale status
tailscale ping <node>
tailscale netcheck
tailscale version

# Auth
sudo tailscale up
sudo tailscale up --authkey <key>
sudo tailscale up --force-reauth

# Tailnet Lock
tailscale lock status
tailscale lock add tlpub:<key>
tailscale lock remove <node-key>   # Owner only

# System extension (Standalone only)
tailscale configure sysext activate
tailscale configure sysext status
tailscale configure sysext deactivate
```

## Admin console — Remove button greyed out

Docs do not spell out every UI reason the **Remove** control is disabled. Check these in order:

1. **Role.** Device removal needs **Owner**, **Admin**, or **IT admin**. Network admin, Billing admin, Auditor, and Member are read-only for devices ([roles](https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/user-roles#roles); [remove a device](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/access-control/device-management/how-to/remove)).
2. **Shared-in node.** Devices shared into this tailnet from another account cannot be deleted with normal device-delete controls ([deleteDevice API](https://tailscale.com/api)).
3. **API delete (Owner / Admin / IT admin)** when the console stays stuck:
```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://api.tailscale.com/api/v2/device/<deviceId>" \
  -u "<api-key>:"
```
Use a masked secret for the API key; never paste it in chat. Replace `<deviceId>` with the node id ([remove a device](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/access-control/device-management/how-to/remove)).
4. If role is correct, the device is not an external share, and console/API still block removal, escalate to [Tailscale Support](https://tailscale.com/contact/support).

## Escalation

When the orchestrator hits a Tailscale issue that requires node-side commands, logging into a console, or `sudo tailscale up --force-reauth`, delegate to the designated recovery agent with the fleet-health file path and the symptom. Only escalate to the Owner if an admin console action is required (key extension, ACL edit) or if the second signing node is also compromised.

skills.name: break-glass-host-troubleshooting
skills.description: use this only when the plugin's HTTP :8642 health/readiness checks prove a host unreachable; allows SSH over Tailscale for host repair, then return to HTTP
skills.content:
# Break-glass host troubleshooting (SSH over Tailscale, repair only)

Golden Rule: read the official Hermes docs for the symptom first (`hermes_docs`). Anything else is labelled "not in official docs".

## Gate: all of these must be true before you use SSH
1. `fleet_health` and `fleet_status` both show <HOST_NAME> as FAIL/RED or unreachable on HTTP :8642. One flaky probe doesn't count: retry once.
2. The likely cause is host-side: the gateway or API server is down, the Tailscale node key expired, the host is wedged after an update or reboot, and so on.
3. The owner says yes to break-glass for that one named host.

If any of these is false, stay on HTTP. Never use SSH to talk to an agent, ask it something, or delegate work to it.

## Repair
- Connect over Tailscale only: `ssh <SSH_USER>@<HOST_NAME>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>`. Never use a public IP, and never paste keys into chat.
- Read first: `hermes status`, `hermes doctor`, `hermes logs`, and `tailscale status`. Use the docs-verified commands for the installed version (`hermes <cmd> --help`).
- If a fix is a mutation, say exactly what you'll run and get a yes first. Make one change at a time. For a gateway restart, follow `hermes-gateway-graceful-restart`. For an expired Tailscale key, follow `tailscale-fleet-macos`.
- Never print secrets, and don't edit `.env` secrets by hand (that's Bitwarden SSOT).

## Exit, straight back to HTTP
- Close the SSH session, then re-run `fleet_health`, `fleet_status`, and `fleet_version` over :8642.
- FAIL LOUD if the host still isn't GREEN. Log what broke and what fixed it (compound-learnings).
